analyst.summary: IDFC First Bank's deposit franchise is a real, ongoing success (CASA 50.8%, retail deposits 79% of the base, up from 27% at merger) but was built at a real cost -- cost-to-income still 72.3% in FY26, versus high-30s/low-40s% for large private peers, and credit-deposit ratio at a tighter 95.5% than most of the sector. The FY25-26 microfinance drag that dominated the narrative is genuinely normalizing: credit cost fell every quarter through FY26 (2.69% to 1.63%) as the MFI book shrank to ~2.3% of loans, and GNPA/NNPA (1.61%/0.48%) are improving, though not yet best-in-class. Q4 FY26's reported PAT of Rs 319 crore masked a messy quarter -- a Rs 483 crore post-tax Chandigarh branch fraud hit (KPMG-confirmed isolated) offset by a Rs 130 crore tax refund, with normalized PAT actually up 145% YoY to Rs 746 crore even as pre-provision operating profit fell 41.6%. The bank's capital position was de-risked via a completed Rs 7,500 crore Warburg Pincus/ADIA preferential raise (CRAR to ~18.9% pro forma), though shareholders notably rejected Warburg's board-seat request. At ~1.4-1.5x book against a mid-single-digit current ROE, the stock is not pricing management's promised mid-teens ROE -- it more closely tracks the Street's own conservative 9-12% recovery case, which makes today's multiple defensible rather than a value trap, but leaves little room for further guidance slippage. Hold.
